questions.question: Following Pie chart presents monthly expenditure by Sushma and Preeti in different heads. Sushma and Preeti make equal expenditure every month. What is the difference between the central angle corresponding to the expenditure incurred on Health by Sushma and Preeti?
questions.questionHtml:
Following Pie chart presents monthly expenditure by Sushma and Preeti in different heads. Sushma and Preeti make equal expenditure every month.


What is the difference between the central angle corresponding to the expenditure incurred on Health by Sushma and Preeti?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Total expenditure each Sushma and Preeti = (1800 + 5000 + 6000 + 7200 + 2500 + 7500)

⇒ 30000

Expenditure incurred on health by Sushma

⇒ 7500

Angle of health expenditure = (7500/30000) × 360

⇒ 90 

Expenditure incurred on health by Preeti

⇒ 20% of 30000

⇒ 6000

Angle of health expenditure

⇒ (6000/30000)× 360

⇒ 72

∴ The difference between the central angle corresponding to the expenditure incurred on Health by Sushma and Preeti = 90 - 72 

⇒ 18°

∴ The difference between the central angle corresponding to the expenditure incurred on Health by Sushma and Preeti is 18°

questions.question: Study the given pie-chart and answer the question that follows. The pie-chart shows the data for A, B, O, AB blood groups of 240 donors. The ratio of the donors of blood group ‘O’ to the average of the donors of groups ‘A’ and ‘AB’ is:
questions.questionHtml:
Study the given pie-chart and answer the question that follows.

The pie-chart shows the data for A, B, O, AB blood groups of 240 donors.

The ratio of the donors of blood group ‘O’ to the average of the donors of groups ‘A’ and ‘AB’ is:
questions.solution:
Given:

240 donors of blood group  A, B , O and AB

Formula used:

360 degrees = Total donors 

Calculation:

As, 360 degree represents 240 donors 

Hence, blood group O has 80 degree 

Blood group O has = 240/360 × 80 donors = 160/3

Now, blood group A represents  90 degree

Blood group A has = 240/360 × 90 = 60 

Now, blood group AB represents 70 degrees

Blood group AB has = 240/360 × 70 = 140/3

Now, average of A and AB = Sum of values/Total number of values = (60 + 140/3) ÷ 2 =  160/3.

Hence, the ratio between O and the average of A and AB = 160/3 : 160/3 = 1:1.

Hence, the ratio is 1:1.

questions.question: The following pie charts represent the distribution of candidates who were enrolled for a competitive examination, and the candidates (out of those enrolled) who passed the exam from five different institutes P, Q, R, S and T. questions.solution:

Total number of candidates passing from P, R and T = \(52\over 100 \) × 4000 = 2,080

Difference = 3,900 - 2,080 = 1,820, Difference % = \(1820\over 2080\) × 100 = 87.5%

questions.solution:
Calculation:

Fuel consumed by light vehicles = (800 × 70/360 × 100) million litres

Total fuel consumed by aviation and waterways = (800 × (90 + 45)/360 × 100) million litres

∴ Required percentage = (800 × 70/360 × 100)/(800 × 135/360 × 100) × 100 = 51.85 ≈ 52%

questions.questionHtml: If 50% of the employees in office E are transferred to office D, then what percentage of the total number of employees of the company is the number of employees in office D?
questions.solution:
Calculation:-

Total employees = 360°

Number of employees in company E = 64.8°

Number of employees in company D = 57.6°

If 50% employees of company E transferred to company D, then number of employees in company D = 57.6° + 64.8°/2 = 57.6° + 32.4° = 90°

Required percentage = [90°/360°] × 100 = 25%

questions.question: The given pie chart show the monthly household expenditure of Family A and Family B under various heads. The monthly expenditures incurred for Family A and Family B are ₹50,000 and ₹75,000, respectively. Study the charts carefully and answer the question that follows. Monthly Household Expenditure of ₹50,000 under various heads of Family A Monthly household expenditure of ₹75,000 under various heads for Family B If the monthly expenditures of both families are combined together then the expenditures on Entertainment of both families together will be what percentage of the total monthly expenditures of both families? Express your answer to the nearest integer.

If the monthly expenditures of both families are combined together then the expenditures on Entertainment of both families together will be what percentage of the total monthly expenditures of both families? Express your answer to the nearest integer.
questions.solution:
Given:

The total monthly Household Expenditure of family A = ₹ 50000

The total monthly Household Expenditure of family B = ₹ 75000

Calculation:

The total expenditures on Entertainment of both families = [(10/100) × 50000] + [(12/100) × 75000]

= 5000 + 9000

= ₹ 14000

The total monthly Household Expenditure of both families = 50000 + 75000 = 125000

The percentage = (14000/125000) × 100 = 11.2% ≈ 11% (nearest integer)

questions.questionHtml:
The savings and expenditure of a family in a month on different heads is shown in the given pie chart. The family saves Rs. 8,000 per month.

Find the total monthly expenditure (in Rs.) of the family.
questions.solution:
Total monthly income = (Monthly savings × 360°) / Angle for savings

Total monthly income = (8,000 × 360) / 60 = 48,000

Total expenditure = Total monthly income - Savings

Total expenditure = 48,000 - 8,000 = 40,000

questions.question: The following pie charts show the data of the number of appeared and passed students of class 12 in sections A, B, C, D and E. How many students failed in Section C?

questions.solution:
Given:

The total number of students appeared = 1800

The total number of students passed = 800

The students appeared from section C = 100° 

The percentage of students passed from section C = 25%

Concept:

\(X\%={X\over100}\)

A circle has total = 360° 

Calculation:

Let the total failed students from section C be X

The total appeared students from section C = \({{100\over360}\times {1800}}={100\times 5}=500\)

The total passed students from section C = \({{25\over100}\times 800}=200\)

The total failed students from section C = X = 500 - 200 = 300

∴ The required result will be 300.

questions.question: The following pie chart shows the number of workers of different categories A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H of a factory in 1995. If the number of workers in category B is increased by 10% and the number of workers in category D is decreased by 5% in 1996, then what is the total number of workers in categories B and D in 1996, if no. of workers in B was 1500 in the year 1995?
questions.questionHtml:
The following pie chart shows the number of workers of different categories A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H of a factory in 1995.

If the number of workers in category B is increased by 10% and the number of workers in category D is decreased by 5% in 1996, then what is the total number of workers in categories B and D in 1996, if no. of workers in B was 1500 in the year 1995?
questions.solution:
Concept Used:

The concept of percentage  is a number or ratio that can be expressed as a fraction of 100

Calculations:

According to the question,

⇒ In 1995, No. of workers is 1500

from the figure, the number of workers in category B is 15%

so, we can say

⇒ 15% = 1500

⇒ 1% = 100

In 1996, Category B increased by 10%

⇒ so, New population of Category B = Original Population x (100 + 10)/100 = 1500 x 110/100 = 15 x 110 = 1650

The number of workers in Category D is 25%

⇒ 1% = 100

⇒ 25% = 2500

In 1996, Category D decreased by 5%

⇒ so, New population of Category D = Original Population x (100 - 5)/100 = 2500 x 95/100 = 25 x 95 = 2375

⇒ Total population of the worker in Category B and Category D = New population of B + New population of D = 1650 + 2375 = 4025

⇒ Hence, The total population of workers in Category B and Category D in 1996 is 4025.

questions.question: The given pie-chart shows the expenditure (in ₹ lakh) of a country on various sports during a particular year. Study the chart carefully and answer the question that follows. The average expenditure on golf and swimming is what per cent (rounded to 1 decimal place) more or less than the average expenditure on football and cricket?
questions.questionHtml:
The given pie-chart shows the expenditure (in ₹ lakh) of a country on various sports during a particular year. Study the chart carefully and answer the question that follows.

The average expenditure on golf and swimming is what per cent (rounded to 1 decimal place) more or less than the average expenditure on football and cricket?
questions.solution:
Solution:

The given angles are:

  • Tennis = 85°
  • Football = 70°
  • Golf = 48°
  • Swimming = 45°
  • Cricket = 60°
  • Basketball = 52°

Step 1: Calculate the average for Golf and Swimming:

Golf + Swimming = 48° + 45° = 93°

Average = 93° / 2 = 46.5°

Step 2: Calculate the average for Football and Cricket:

Football + Cricket = 70° + 60° = 130°

Average = 130° / 2 = 65°

Step 3: Calculate the percentage difference:

Percentage difference = ((65° - 46.5°) / 65°) × 100 = 28.5%

Final Answer: The average expenditure on Golf and Swimming is 28.5% less than the average expenditure on Football and Cricket.

θ/360° = 8/100 (percentage is taken out of 100, similarly angle is calculated on 360°)

⇒ θ/360° = 2/25

⇒ θ = 360 × (2/25)

⇒ θ = 28.8° 

∴ The correct choice is option 4.

questions.question: If it is known that 35 students mentioned momos as their preferred food, on the basis of the information provided in the following pie chart, calculate the number of students who mentioned both rolls and Alu Parathas as their preferred food.
questions.questionHtml: If it is known that 35 students mentioned momos as their preferred food, on the basis of the information provided in the following pie chart, calculate the number of students who mentioned both rolls and Alu Parathas as their preferred food.
questions.solution:
Given:

Number of students mentioned momos as their preferred food = 35

Concept Used:

Share of different items = Share of one part × Share of the given item

Calculation:

⇒ Fraction share for momos = 0.125

⇒ Number of students for the momos = 35

⇒ Students in the fraction share of momos for 0.1 part = \(\frac{35}{0.125}\times 0.1 =28\)

⇒ Fraction share for Rolls = 0.2

⇒ Fraction share for Alu Paranthas = 0.2

⇒ Total fraction part = 0.2 + 0.2 = 0.4

⇒ Students in the total fraction part of rolls and alu paranthas = \(\frac{28}{0.1}\times 0.4 = 112\)

Hence, the total number of students who mentioned either rolls or alu paranthas as their preferred food is 112

questions.question: If the price of guava is Rs. 12 per kg, that of mango is Rs. 30 per kg, that of apple is Rs. 40 per kg, that of orange is Rs. 20 per kg and that of banana is Rs. 15 per kg, then what is the total cost of all fruits at shop B?
questions.questionHtml: If the price of guava is Rs. 12 per kg, that of mango is Rs. 30 per kg, that of apple is Rs. 40 per kg, that of orange is Rs. 20 per kg and that of banana is Rs. 15 per kg, then what is the total cost of all fruits at shop B?
questions.solution:
Given:

The price of guava is Rs. 12 per kg 8

 The price of mango is Rs. 30 per kg 18

The price of an apple is Rs. 40 per kg  22

 The price of orange is Rs. 20 per kg  24

The price of banana is Rs. 15 per kg  28

Calculation:

The total cost of fruits from shop B = Sum of (Quantity of fruit × rate of fruit per kg ) of all fruits

The total cost of fruits from shop B = 1200 × 8% × 12 + 1200 × 18% × 30 + 1200 × 22% × 40 + 1200 × 24% × 20 + 1200 × 28% × 15

The total cost of fruits from shop B = 1200 × (0.96 + 5.4 + 8.8 + 4.8 + 4.2) = Rs 28,992

∴ The total cost is Rs 28,992.

questions.solution:

Percentage of popularity of Anjeer flavour out of 'Other' = 20% 

No of people liking Anjeer flavour = 4082 

Calculation: 

Let the no of people surveyed = y 

As per the question;

⇒ y × 15.7% = 'Other' category 

No of people liking Anjeer flavour = 4082 

⇒ (y × 15.7%) × 20% = 4082 

⇒ y × 157/1000 × 20/100 = 4082 

⇒ y × 157/1000 × 1/5 = 4082 

⇒ y = (4082 × 1000 × 5)/157

⇒ y = 130000 

∴ The no of people surveyed was 130000.

Alternate MethodBy unitary method:

20% = 4082

⇒ 1% = 4082/20

The number of people liking other = 100%

⇒ 100 × (4082/20)

⇒ 20410

Now, according to the pie chart,

15.7% of the total is 20410.

⇒ 15.7% = 20410

⇒ 1% = 20410/15.7

⇒ 100% = (20410/15.7) × 100

⇒ 130000

∴ The no of people surveyed was 130000.

questions.question: Study the following pie-chart carefully and answer the given question. The pie-chart represents the marks obtained by Sanya in different subjects in class 12. Total marks scored by her in class 12 was 450. Marks obtained If the total central angles corresponding to the pair of subjects (Physics and Hindi), (Chemistry and Physics) and (Hindi and Chemistry) were 156°, 144° and 140°, respectively, then find the total marks obtained by her in (English and Biology).
questions.questionHtml:
Study the following pie-chart carefully and answer the given question. The pie-chart represents the marks obtained by Sanya in different subjects in class 12. Total marks scored by her in class 12 was 450. 

               Marks obtained

If the total central angles corresponding to the pair of subjects (Physics and Hindi), (Chemistry and Physics) and (Hindi and Chemistry) were 156°, 144° and 140°, respectively, then find the total marks obtained by her in (English and Biology).
questions.solution:
Given:

Total marks scored by Sanya = 450

Central angles:

  • (Physics and Hindi) = 156°
  • (Chemistry and Physics) = 144°
  • (Hindi and Chemistry) = 140°

Formula used:

Total central angle = 360°

Marks corresponding to a subject = (Central angle of the subject / Total central angle) × Total marks

Calculation:

Sum of central angles for Physics, Chemistry, and Hindi = (156° + 144° + 140°) / 2 = 220°

Central angle for English and Biology = 360° - 220°

⇒ Central angle for English and Biology = 140°

Marks for English and Biology = (140 / 360) × 450

⇒ Marks = (7 / 18) × 450

⇒ Marks = 175

∴ The total marks obtained by Sanya in English and Biology is 175 marks.

questions.question: Study the given pie-charts and answer the question that follows. The pie-charts show the characteristics of foreign tourists visiting India during a given year. If in a given year, 2,50,000 tourists visited India and the age wise distribution of data applies to all the countries, then what is the ratio of American tourists below 10 years to the other tourists above 50 years?
questions.questionHtml:
Study the given pie-charts and answer the question that follows.

The pie-charts show the characteristics of foreign tourists visiting India during a given year.

If in a given year, 2,50,000 tourists visited India and the age wise distribution of data applies to all the countries, then what is the ratio of American tourists below 10 years to the other tourists above 50 years?
questions.solution:
Given:

Total number of tourists = 2,50,000

Country-wise distribution:

  • American = 40%
  • British = 25%
  • Russian = 15%
  • Others = 20%

Age-wise distribution:

  • Below 10 years = 15%
  • Between 10-30 years = 25%
  • Between 31-50 years = 50%
  • Above 50 years = 10%

Step 1: Find the number of American tourists below 10 years.

American tourists = 40% of 2,50,000 = (40/100) × 2,50,000 = 1,00,000

American tourists below 10 years = 15% of 1,00,000 = (15/100) × 1,00,000 = 15,000

Step 2: Find the number of other tourists above 50 years.

Other tourists = 20% of 2,50,000 = (20/100) × 2,50,000 = 50,000

Other tourists above 50 years = 10% of 50,000 = (10/100) × 50,000 = 5,000

Step 3: Find the required ratio.

Ratio = American tourists below 10 years : Other tourists above 50 years

⇒ Ratio = 15,000 : 5,000

⇒ Ratio = 3 : 1

∴ The ratio of American tourists below 10 years to other tourists above 50 years is 3:1.
